flows.title: The whole project, in four parts
flows.intro: The website asks. The server decides. The database remembers.
steps: Someone searches, books, publishes or reviews an event. Each role has different permissions.
The screen collects input and shows results. It does not decide whether a payment is genuine or whether stock can be reserved.
The server validates input, checks the user and applies the feature rules. It calls other services only when needed.
Users, events, bookings, payments and tickets live here. Transactions and constraints protect important relationships.
rules: Redis helps with speed and AI limits; it is not the inventory authority.
Cloudinary stores images; Brevo sends email; Razorpay handles payments; Groq generates AI text.

flows.title: What happens when I search?
flows.intro: Follow one search from the screen to the event cards.
steps: For example: music events in Delhi. The frontend puts these choices into the API request.
The API accepts supported input and passes it to the event service. Public browsing does not require a booking account.
The service applies filters, a stable ordering and a page size. SQL selects records; Prisma loads their related information.
Each summary includes the event name, image, venue and lowest active ticket price. Missing price is not a free ticket.
The same card design can appear on different pages. Price is stored in paise and formatted into rupees for display.
rules: Server pagination avoids downloading the entire catalog at once.
Related-event cards need the same price fields as ordinary search cards.

flows.title: How does the website know who I am?
flows.intro: Identity and permission are separate checks.
steps: The server verifies the sign-in method. A stored password is hashed, not kept as readable text.
A signed access token identifies the request. A separate refresh cookie supports renewal; its token hash is stored server-side.
The frontend attaches the access token. On an expired-token response it can attempt a refresh and retry.
A valid user still cannot edit another organizer’s event. Hiding a button is not a security check.
The backend performs the permitted action or returns an error. Account status can be checked again on a later request.
rules: Authentication: who are you? Authorization: may you do this?
JWT contents are signed, not encrypted. The system also uses database session state.

flows.title: How a ticket becomes yours
flows.intro: A reservation and a successful payment are different things.
steps: The browser sends ticket IDs, quantities and an idempotency key. Its displayed total is not trusted as the final charge.
The server loads active ticket prices and validates the event, sale window and requested quantities.
Stock is decreased only when enough remains. The booking and stock changes commit together, or roll back together.
The server verifies provider information from checkout verification or a signed webhook. A browser success screen alone is not proof.
A valid confirmation changes the booking and issues tickets once. Repeated messages must not create another set of tickets.
rules: If the reservation expires, a guarded transition returns stock.
A repeated request or webhook must not repeat the business outcome.

flows.title: How the assistant finds a useful answer
flows.intro: First understand the request. Then find facts. Then answer.
steps: A greeting, a mood request and a question about one event are different requests. Recent conversation is kept within a budget.
City, date, budget and group size
The assistant turns preferences into validated filters. Similar meaning does not justify ignoring price or availability.
MiniLM produces vectors that help match meaning. Event-specific passages can also be selected using lexical and semantic scores.
Selected text passages and structured facts give the model context. Numeric vectors are used for matching, not as a replacement for those facts.
Application checks and live catalog information constrain the result. Clarification or a fallback may be needed instead of a confident guess.
rules: This is a learning map: an interpretation call may happen before retrieval.
RAG does not fine-tune the model, remove token limits or guarantee a correct answer.
flows.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1216" height="620" viewBox="0 0 1216 620" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc"><title id="title">How the assistant finds a useful answer</title><desc id="desc">1. flows.title: How code reaches the website
flows.intro: GitHub checks and hosting deployments are related, but separate.
steps: A commit records a revision. Pushing it publishes that revision to the remote repository.
GitHub stores the code and study files. Other people or AI tools can read the learning guide from this revision.
Lint, types, tests and build checks examine a revision. One failed step can fail the job and stop later steps.
Hosting services build and run the frontend and API using their configuration. Do not assume the diagram means CI always gates deployment.
Runtime health also depends on environment settings, database access and external providers. A green check is not a runtime trace.
rules: A CI failure does not mean all individual tests failed.
A passing CI run does not by itself prove that the latest deployment is healthy.

technologyRows: Shared types across UI, API and packages
Typed contracts help refactoring. Types disappear at runtime, so incoming data still needs validation. Plain JS reduces type setup but loses compile-time checking.
Routing, layouts, server page loading and interactive client components
Integrated page rendering and routing fit a browsable event catalog. Vite is attractive for a browser-only SPA; it is not an inferior choice for every app.
Local UI state, auth state and shared pending counters

Current state is mostly local or small shared contexts. Redux/Zustand can organise more complex shared state; a query library can formalise server-state caching and invalidation. Context is not a full query cache.
Responsive layout, colour tokens, surface layers and reusable controls
Utility styles coexist with custom product CSS. A component framework supplies more ready-made patterns but also brings its own conventions.
HTTP server, middleware, REST routes and feature controllers

Express keeps the HTTP layer explicit and small. Nest offers more enforced conventions; Fastify offers a different plugin/schema approach. Current source uses Express even where classes retain decorator-like helper syntax.
Feature separation inside one API deployment

Keeps transactions and deployment understandable at this scale. Microservices enable independent ownership/deployment, but introduce network failures, service coordination and distributed data concerns.
Explicit feature endpoints fit the clients here. GraphQL supports flexible client selection; tRPC offers tightly coupled TS inference; gRPC fits other internal service contexts.
Runtime input validation and shared schemas
One TypeScript-friendly schema layer can validate unknown input. Runtime validation complements types rather than replacing authorization or database constraints.
Authoritative relational data, transactions, constraints, full-text search and embedding arrays

Events, bookings, ticket types and payments form a relational model. MySQL is a credible relational alternative. MongoDB also supports multi-document transactions; the reason here is relational fit and query requirements, not an inability to transact.
Typed database access, schema/migrations and transactions
Helps navigate related records while retaining parameterized SQL for FTS and ranking. Raw SQL offers direct control but more manual mapping; ORM use does not remove the need to understand SQL.
Keyword discovery, filtering and ordered result pages
Reuses the database for current catalog needs. A dedicated search service can add richer relevance operations but needs indexing, freshness handling and another system to operate.
Public-read TTL caches and shared AI rate/concurrency protection

Shared state can span API instances. An in-memory Map is simpler but instance-local. Redis is not the authority for booking prices or inventory. Public caches can degrade gracefully; AI protection deliberately has different failure behaviour.
Inventory reservation and guarded booking transitions
Explicit row locks; optimistic versioning; queue-based serialisation
The stock condition is part of the write, so concurrent buyers cannot both consume the final unit. Other approaches can also be correct; compare contention, retries and operational complexity.
Provider orders, checkout verification, webhook handling and refund lifecycle

INR-oriented event checkout fits the integration. Provider choice depends on supported markets, onboarding and product requirements. Do not claim test/demo payments are real captured customer revenue.
JWT + rotating refresh sessions + Argon2id + Google OAuth
Account authentication, refresh and password protection
Server-session cookies; managed auth such as Auth0/Clerk

Explicit auth demonstrates session and ownership rules. Managed auth reduces custom lifecycle work; opaque sessions are a valid alternative. The current system already uses database session state, so it is not fully stateless.
Organizer uploads, category covers and hosted image delivery

Media is kept outside the API filesystem. Object storage offers greater infrastructure control but needs a delivery/processing design. Multiple configured providers still require consistent ownership and asset tracking.
Verification codes, password reset and transactional notifications
A hosted mail service avoids operating an SMTP server. Delivery still needs sender/domain configuration, retry handling and user-visible failure states.
Intent interpretation, response generation and model-profile routing
Other hosted LLM providers; self-hosted models

Existing integration centralises budgets, retry policy and grounded output handling. Switching providers would require evaluating quality, latency, cost, tool support and failure behaviour; the repository alone cannot prove one provider is universally best.
Local semantic embeddings for event and passage retrieval
Hosted embedding APIs; larger local encoders
Local CPU inference avoids per-embedding external API calls but brings model download, cold-start, CPU and memory costs. Local does not mean computationally free.
Store and compare current catalog vectors
pgvector with an index; Qdrant; Pinecone; Weaviate

Keeps the current small catalog in one database. Exact scanning is simpler but does not have the scaling behaviour of approximate indexed vector search. pgvector is an extension, not something already used just because PostgreSQL holds vectors.
Combine business filters, semantic retrieval, lexical passage selection and bounded prompt context
Keyword-only search; full-catalog prompts; LangChain/LlamaIndex orchestration

Custom code makes this small workflow explicit. Orchestration libraries can supply connectors and common patterns, but are not prerequisites for RAG. RAG retrieves evidence; it does not fine-tune the model or remove token limits.
Present tickets and read them at admission
Barcode; manual booking lookup; native scanner
A QR is convenient to transport an identifier. Backend authorization and ticket status checks determine admission; possessing a readable QR alone does not establish permission.
Current charts need a small set of interactions. A library becomes useful for richer plots, zooming or larger datasets. Do not claim the project uses a chart library it does not import.
Automated regressions, database checks and build checks
Vitest; other CI providers; browser E2E tooling

Existing tests cover backend logic and PostgreSQL-backed scenarios. Test-tool installation does not establish complete browser coverage. CI success is distinct from service deployment and production correctness.
Shared packages and dependency-aware task orchestration
A monorepo keeps shared contracts and app changes together. It adds task/build coordination; it does not automatically mean microservices or one deployed process.
Frontend/API/database hosting and the public domain

Managed hosting suits the portfolio deployment. More infrastructure control brings operational responsibility. Build-time public variables, CORS, TLS, cold starts and database connection limits remain relevant.
Error capture with sensitive-data scrubbing and request correlation
The integration exists; enabled collection depends on configuration. Logs and traces answer different questions, and sensitive data should not become a debugging shortcut.
roadmap: Who are the three user roles? Trace one click from browser to database and back.
Promises, async/await, closures, objects and arrays; why doesn't a TS interface validate JSON?
Methods, status codes, request/response bodies, middleware, validation and error handling?
State vs props; controlled inputs; effect dependencies; cleanup; why can navigation replay an initial prompt?
Why is the homepage a server component while the chat composer needs client state? What can run in each?
How does async I/O differ from parallel CPU work? Why can local embedding inference affect latency?
Why BookingItem? Which relationships are one-to-many? What do unique constraints and indexes protect?
JWT vs session; password hashing vs encryption; refresh rotation; ownership checks; cookie and local-storage tradeoffs?
Why server pagination? Stable sorting? FTS vs substring search? Offset vs cursor pagination?
Cache-aside, TTL and invalidation? What remains correct if Redis fails? What is intentionally rejected?
Two people buy the final ticket: why does a conditional update matter? What rolls back on partial failure?
Duplicate booking clicks? Reused keys across users? Expiry and confirmation arriving together?
Why not trust browser success? What do signatures protect? How do duplicate, delayed or out-of-order events behave?
What is retrieved? Why send text rather than vectors to generation? Keyword vs semantic search? Why not send all events?
Hard filters, unsupported claims, clarification, language, retries, prompt injection, budgets and stale evidence?
Why can one failed test fail the run? CI vs deployment? Where are environment variables read? How would you roll back?
CORS vs authorization, XSS/CSRF, rate limits, logging sensitive data, request IDs and diagnosing latency?
When split services? When use pgvector/indexing? Why would a durable queue help? What breaks with several API instances?
Responsive layouts, keyboard focus, chart interactions, image aspect ratios, upload ownership and loading states?
DNS vs application hosting, TLS, API origin, email sender authentication and third-party outages?
glossary: API
The HTTP interface the frontend uses to ask the backend to do work
ORM
Prisma's typed interface to database queries and relationships
Transaction
A group of database changes that commits or rolls back together
Invariant
A condition that must stay true, such as inventory never becoming negative
Idempotency
Repeating the same intended operation does not create another outcome
JWT
A signed access token; signing does not encrypt its contents
TTL
How long a cached value or reservation remains valid
Webhook
A provider-to-server event notification, independent of the browser
Embedding
A numeric representation used to compare semantic similarity
RAG
Retrieve relevant facts, then use those facts to ground a generated answer
Modular monolith
One backend deployment with separate feature modules
CI
Automated checks of a proposed revision; distinct from deployment
